hero.subtitle: A fall at a Garvey Avenue market or an Atlantic Boulevard shopping plaza can leave you with more questions than answers. We help injured Monterey Park residents pursue premises liability claims. Our team understands local hazards and how to build a strong case.

about.title: Monterey Park Slip & Fall Claims
about.longDescription: Monterey Park's mix of dense commercial corridors, shopping plazas, and older apartment complexes near Garfield Avenue and Garvey Avenue means uneven walkways, wet floors, and poorly lit stairwells are common hazards. When a property owner fails to notice or fix a dangerous condition, California law may hold them responsible for resulting injuries. But proving that a business or landlord knew or reasonably should have known about a hazard takes evidence gathered quickly, before spills get mopped up and surveillance footage gets erased. We handle premises liability claims throughout Monterey Park, from Atlantic Boulevard storefronts to SR-60 corridor businesses. Our team can evaluate the circumstances of your fall and help pursue a fair claim. There's no cost or obligation for an initial review, and we work on contingency, meaning fees apply only if there's a recovery.

whyChoose.title: Why Documentation Matters in a Monterey Park Fall Case

items.title: Notice Is Everything
items.desc: California requires showing the property owner knew or should have known about the hazard and failed to address it. We can help gather maintenance logs, prior complaints, or inspection records to establish that notice.

items.title: Surveillance Video Disappears Fast
items.desc: Many Monterey Park businesses overwrite security footage within days or weeks. Acting quickly to request preservation of video can be critical to reconstructing what happened.

items.title: Comparative Fault Doesn't Bar Recovery
items.desc: Under California's pure comparative fault rule, even if you were partly responsible for the fall, you may still recover a reduced share of damages rather than being shut out entirely.

items.question: How long do I have to file a slip and fall claim in Monterey Park?
items.answer: Generally, California gives you two years from the date of the fall to file a lawsuit. If the property involved is owned by a government entity, such as a city building or public sidewalk, the deadline is much shorter and requires a separate claims process. It's best to speak with us as soon as possible to avoid missing any deadline.

items.question: What if I fell at a store on Atlantic Boulevard or Garvey Avenue and didn't report it right away?
items.answer: Not reporting immediately doesn't automatically end your options, but it can make proving the hazard existed more difficult. Photos of the scene, witness names, and any available surveillance footage become even more important. We can help figure out what evidence may still be recoverable.

items.question: Does it cost anything to find out if I have a case?
items.answer: No. Our initial case review is free, and there's no obligation to move forward. We typically work on contingency, meaning you pay nothing upfront and fees apply only if you recover compensation.
